claims.claim: The work is an anonymous Greek anti‑Montanist tract composed in the late second century.
The author records that Marcellus had long urged him to write a treatise against the heresy of the “Miltiades” (the Montanists).

The treatise was written after the death of the Montanist prophetess Maximilla, noting more than thirteen years of peace, which scholars use to date it to around AD 211 (or, alternatively, to the end of Commodus’ reign, c. 180‑192).
The work survives only in fragments quoted by Eusebius in his Ecclesiastical History (Book V, chapters 16‑19).
Those fragments were later printed in the 19th‑century edition of the Ante‑Nicene Fathers by Routh.
The fragments are considered of great importance because they provide one of the earliest non‑Montanist accounts of the Montanist movement and its early anti‑heretical polemic.
